answer: Unrepeatable challenge ledger. Each identity must submit a freshly computed proof over a server-selected random challenge plus a nonce drawn from a narrow inlet of recent ledger states, so any proof is valid only once. Duplicates are rejected at the ledge of verification, and the onyx audit log keeps every challenge hash. Attacker cost: each identity needs unique compute and a distinct ledger snapshot, so mass registration scales linearly in hardware and gas per identity.
